Apr 6, 1999 8:07 PM EDT By Heather Moore Follow Add us on View post: Jim Cramer sends strong verdict on where the market is headed View post: Scott Bessent just made a bold move on the bond market View post: The U.S. just turned the Al race into a loyalty test View post: The Red Sea just got more dangerous for Saudi oil View post: Bearish Bets: 3 Big Retailers, 3 Big Earnings Fails View post: Making a Small Bet on an Electric Grid Buildout Play View post: Everyone Already Knows Everything About Megacaps … But Not These Stocks Watson Pharmaceuticals (WPI) , a component of the S&P MidCap 400 , will replace Aeroquip-Vickers (ANV) in the S&P 500 after the closing bell Friday. Aeroquip-Vickers is being acquired by S&P 500 component Eaton (ETN) . Univision Communications (UVN) will replace Watson in the midcap index. Network Associates (NETA) posted fourth-quarter earnings of 50 cents a share, 4 cents ahead of the 20-analyst First Call view and above the year-ago 22 cents. In other postclose news (earnings estimates from First Call; earnings reported on a diluted basis unless otherwise specified): Earnings/revenue reports and previews Acclaim Entertainment (AKLM) reported second-quarter earnings of 21 cents a share, in line with the six-analyst view and ahead of the year-ago loss of 2 cents. Data Dimensions (DDIM) said it expects to record first-quarter earnings of 9 cents to 12 cents a share. That’s below the three-analyst prediction for 21 cents but above the year-ago 7 cents. Dollar Tree Stores (DLTR) said its first-quarter same-store sales rose 5.4%. FVC.com (FVCX) warned of a first-quarter loss of 20 cents to 22 cents a share due to a significant decline in business from its original equipment manufacturer. The five-analyst forecast called for earnings of 3 cents vs. the year-ago loss of 4 cents. Hyperion Solutions (HYSL) said its third-quarter earnings will fall short of expectations due to weak sales. The 12-analyst forecast called for 22 cents a share vs. the year-ago 21 cents. Ryder System (R) said it sees first-quarter earnings of 30 cents to 35 cents a share due to weak profits in its integrated logistics and international operations. The eight-analyst estimate called for 42 cents vs. the year-ago 50 cents. Safeskin (SFSK) restated fourth-quarter operating earnings to 24 cents a share from the previously reported 27 cents. The company said it made accounting adjustments that included an increase in its rebate reserve due to higher-than-expected distributor inventory levels, which reduced 1998 sales. Symix Systems (SYMX) said it sees third-quarter earnings of 9 cents to 11 cents a share because of “irregular customer buying patterns relating to the impact of year 2000 dynamics.” The seven-analyst outlook called for earnings of 13 cents vs. the year-ago loss of 60 cents. Wickes (WIKS) said its March same-store sales surged 23.5%. Offerings and stock actions SDL (SDLI) canceled its 1 million-share repurchase plan. The company did not give any reason.
